mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% over two months signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances where HOUST dropped by more than 10% over two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month indicates a weakening labor market, which typically precedes broader economic weakness and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE increased by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over two months signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO increased by more than 1% over two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) over three months signals deflationary pressures, which typically lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate revenues and profit margins are squeezed.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the periods where CPIAUCSL showed a sustained decline over three months.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 over a month, it signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer spending and confidence rise.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where PAYEMS increased by more than 200,000 over a month.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by more than 1% month-over-month, it signals strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where RSAFS increased by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) both increase by more than 0.5% within a month, it signals a tightening monetary policy with inflationary pressures, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns are eroded.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both increase > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the instances where both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL increased by more than 0.5% within a month.
